kind: A choice of reading, made on the first million validation bytes and then scored on test and validation: v19's stack (fsp-st) with its reads reaching 16,384 or 32,768 cells back. No training.
why: The stack remembers better than the Transformer at every distance: at the reach of 8,192 it is 0.074 bits a byte ahead on copies from the last 2,032 bytes and 0.411 ahead on copies that only its reach finds (full_size_best_rate_pair.json). The pair chose its reach between two values, the trained 2,048 and 8,192, and 8,192 was 0.0166 better on the first validation million (1.17391 against 1.19049). A stack reads a stream, so its reach is a choice of reading, as it was when 8,192 was chosen; its forgetting slopes were built to extend the ages of its cells beyond the trained window. The Transformer's windows are fixed by its training: it has learned positions up to 2,048 bytes. Longer reaches were never tried at full size.
measure: As the pair's scan: the averaged weights of fsp-st (the release file, weights identical to the scored file) on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 unscored lead bytes, without fast output synapses, on the laptop's GPU; the reach of 8,192 is scored again on the same device beside them, so that every reach is compared on one device. If a longer reach is chosen, the full test and validation splits are scored at that reach with fast output synapses on all levels at 2^24, as the pair scored its stack, and paired with fsp-tf (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 2,032, far 8,192 and far 32,768).
reading: The reach with the lowest score on the first validation million among 2,048, 8,192, 16,384 and 32,768 is the stack's reading. If it is longer than 8,192, its test and validation scores with fast output synapses are reported as the stack's best reading and paired with the Transformer, beside the pair's pre-registered reading at 8,192, whose verdict in full_size_best_rate_pair.json stands as recorded. If 8,192 stays best, longer reaches are reported and dropped. Every later stack's scan includes the reaches of 16,384 and 32,768.
seen_before_recording: full_size_best_rate_pair.json with its result, the pair's scans at 2,048 and 8,192, and the split by context at 8,192. No longer reach of any full-size stack has been scored.

amendment.change: Before any scan has a score. The scans move from the laptop's GPU to the server's, where the pair's own scans ran (on the pair's code copy, v17l), so that the reach of 8,192 needs no second scan: its control is the pair's scan-8192 (1.17391). The reaches of 16,384 and 32,768 are queued as scheduler jobs on GPU 0 in the window of 2026-11-24/25. Arms, measure and reading are unchanged.
